model: NBFC FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, equity retention at the leverage corridor

equity_bridge.item: Oct-2026 capital raise proceeds (QIP Rs 11,700cr + Bajaj Finserv warrants Rs 5,800cr), assumed fully received
equity_bridge.note: Board approval 2026-10-01, subject to shareholders; matched by 167m new shares in projected_shares. Warrants are 25% paid up-front and 75% on conversion within 18 months; treated as converted. Remove both legs if the raise lapses.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Near-term revenue path: FY27 total-income growth ~21% (H1 FY27 +21.3%, AUM +26% with yield repricing and mortgage mix taking ~5 pts off), fading to 17% by FY29. Not the equity CAGR (28%), which is inflated by the FY25 BHFL IPO/OFS proceeds and the leverage build.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 28.0% vs EPS 3yr CAGR 17.2%: >30% divergence. FY2023 EPS sat on a cyclically low credit cost (0.96% of AUF) while FY2026 EPS carries 2.09% including the accelerated ECL; equity was lifted by the Sep-2024 BHFL IPO/OFS and retained earnings at ~18-19% ROE. The 5yr CAGRs (EPS 33%, equity 25%) are both distorted by the FY2021 COVID trough base. Revenue 25% is the cleaner history.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are null by design: reported FCF is loan-book growth for a lender and the FCFE series (profit less retention) is near zero in every fast-growth year, so a CAGR on it is noise. Total income has compounded 33% over 19 years (company snapshot) and 25% over 3 and 5 years; PAT 46% over 19 years.

scenario_narratives.base: Bajaj Finance keeps delivering its published financial-sustainability framework: AUM 23-25% for the next 3-4 years fading toward system growth, ROA 4.3-4.7%, ROE 19-21%, GNPA under 1.4%. Total income grows ~5 pts slower than AUM near term as the mortgage share rises and floating-rate loans reprice down, then converges. Growth is funded first by the Oct-2026 Rs 17,500cr raise and then by retained earnings inside a 5.0-5.5x leverage corridor, which keeps FCFE near zero in FY27 and lets it build to ~16% of income by FY36 as growth slows. Discounted at a 13% INR cost of equity.
scenario_narratives.bull: Growth runs at the top of guidance for longer, credit costs settle at the 1.3-1.5% vintage trend, FINAI delivers visible opex leverage, and the deposit/AAA funding franchise earns bank-like cost of equity (12.5%) with 6.5% perpetual growth.
scenario_narratives.bear: A consumer-credit cycle in FY28-29 plus structural spread compression from banks, fintechs and captive financiers; PBT margin resets to 31%, growth to high single digits, leverage forced lower, cost of equity 14%, perpetual growth 5%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A lender is valued on the cash it can distribute after funding its own growth at a prudent leverage, discounted at the cost of equity. For Bajaj Finance that flow is small today and large later: at 20% ROE and 21-26% growth almost every rupee of profit must be retained (or raised), so the value sits in the terminal franchise. The model gives full credit to a 10-year fade from 21% to 6.5% growth at a ~34% pre-tax margin and ~18-20% ROE, which is a generous operating case, and charges 13% for the risk. The market price embeds a cost of equity near 9-10% or a perpetual ROE spread the model does not grant; the folder's large Indian private banks (HDB, IBN) show the same ~30% gap at 12.5% and this franchise trades at a far higher multiple of book than they do.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit cycle: every 50bp of sustained loan loss/AUF is ~3 pts of total-income margin and ~Rs 60-70/share of value
Cost of equity: the valuation is more sensitive to the 13% discount rate than to any operating driver; at ~9.5% the base case reaches the market price
Terminal retention/leverage: RBI scale-based regulation or a lower leverage tolerance (kappa 1.5 vs 1.4) cuts the terminal payout
Capital-raise pricing: the Rs 17,500cr raise is modelled at ~Rs 1,050/share; a lower QIP price adds shares at a discount to the pro forma value
Competition in durables/personal loans from banks, fintechs and captive financiers compressing yields faster than cost of funds falls
Regulatory action on digital lending products (repeat of the Nov-2023 eCOM/Insta EMI Card ban) interrupting new-customer growth

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (NSE regular close); 52-week range 787.9-1176.4
data_sources.financials: BAJFINANCE.NS_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, Ind AS consolidated FY2009-FY2026 annual, Q3 FY23-Q2 FY27 quarterly; EPS and shares restated to Rs 1 face value), BAJFINANCE.NS_Annual_FY2026.txt consolidated statements and notes 23/24/37/38, BAJFINANCE.NS_Presentation_Q2-FY2027_20261019.txt (19-year snapshot, H1 FY27 P&L, capital raise, leverage, CRAR)
data_sources.qualitative: BAJFINANCE.NS_Analysis.json (guidance corridors, capital raise, board changes, RBI action history)

inputs.share_count_basis: Pro forma fully diluted, equity shares of Rs 1 face value. 6,217.9m outstanding at 2026-03-31 (6,222.48m issued less 4.6m held by the BFL Employee Welfare Trust, FY2026 AR note 23) + 19.9m treasury-method ESOP dilution (FY26 diluted weighted 6,233.97m less basic 6,214.05m, note 38) = 6,238m, PLUS 167m new shares for the Rs 17,500 crore capital raise approved by the Board on 2026-10-01 (QIP up to Rs 11,700cr + Rs 5,800cr promoter warrants to Bajaj Finserv), assumed fully placed/converted at ~Rs 1,050/share (SEBI ICDR floor ~ 2-week VWAP). The proceeds sit in equity_bridge so the raise is charged once: more shares, more cash. Held flat thereafter: ESOP cost is expensed inside the flows (sbc_pct_path), so option exercises are not also modelled as dilution. REFRESH the share count and the bridge to the actual allotment price once the QIP/warrant allotments are filed; a lower issue price is mildly dilutive to IV/share.
inputs.sbc_source: Consolidated cash flow statement add-back, share-based payment to employees, FY2026 Rs 439.6 crore (Metrics.csv StockBasedComp FY2026 = 4,396m; FY25 3,939.8m, FY24 2,682.3m). Indian ESOPs settle in new shares via the Employee Welfare Trust; no net-share-settlement tax line exists, so EquityAwardTaxes = 0.
inputs.fcf_definition: NBFC free cash flow to equity, not owner FCF. last_fcf = FY2026 profit attributable to owners (Rs 190,174m, after SBC, after the BHFL non-controlling interest) less the equity retention needed to fund FY26 revenue growth at kappa = 1.40 x the Rs 122,989m revenue increase (= Rs 172,189m) = Rs 17,985m. reported_fcf adds the SBC back (street basis). The company's reported operating cash flow (-Rs 657,898m) is loan-book growth and is not a valuation input. Interest income is the lender's revenue, not an excess-cash return, so interest_income = 0. Borrowings (Rs 4.35trn) and deposits (Rs 685bn) are operating funding of the loan book, not a capital-structure choice: net_debt = 0 and nothing is deducted after the flows, which are already post-interest.
inputs.retention_definition: capex_pct_path is NOT capex. It is the equity the lender must retain to grow: kappa x g/(1+g) percent of revenue, where kappa is owners' equity / total income. FY2026 actual kappa = 113,999 / 81,989 = 1.39 (consolidated leverage 4.8x; 5.1x at Sep-2026 against management's 5.0x-5.5x corridor). Base 1.40 (corridor held, assets/revenue drifts up as mortgages grow), bull 1.35 (top of corridor), bear 1.50 (RBI tightening / lower leverage tolerance). Implied ROE on average equity ~20% in FY27 fading to ~18% in the terminal year (base).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T09:59:15Z (NSE regular close, 15:29 IST Friday 6 Nov 2026; valuation written Sunday 8 Nov)
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2026-03-31 (latest audited consolidated balance sheet; the Q2 FY27 presentation of 2026-10-19 gives leverage 5.1x, CRAR 20.33%, Tier-1 19.43% at 2026-09-30 but no consolidated net worth line, so equity anchors are 31-Mar-2026 plus H1 retained profit implicitly via the flows)
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-03-31 plus pro forma Oct-2026 capital raise
inputs.base_year_notes: FY2026 consolidated: total income Rs 81,989cr; NTI 53,323cr; opex 17,776cr (33.3% of NTI); loan losses 9,482cr (2.09% of avg AUF, incl. ~1,548cr accelerated ECL 'for long-term resilience' booked in Q3 FY26); PBT 25,817cr (adjusted 27,630cr, +23%); PAT 19,332cr (adjusted 20,689cr), of which 19,017cr to owners and 315cr to the ~13% BHFL minority; adjusted ROA 4.56%, adjusted ROE 19.22%. The Rs 1,416cr gain on the BHFL stake sale is an equity transaction in the consolidated accounts (Ind AS 110) and is excluded; the -265cr New Labour Codes exceptional is excluded from the margin anchor. H1 FY27: total income Rs 47,741cr (+21%), PBT 16,686cr (35.0% of income), PAT 12,447cr (26.1%), AUM +26% to 584,624cr, loan loss/AUF 1.56% in Q2.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in INR, the currency of the flows: India 10Y G-sec ~6.5% (Oct-2026 level used for HDB/IBN) + ~6.5% equity risk premium x beta ~1.0 = 13.0% base. 50bp above the 12.5% used for HDFC Bank / ICICI Bank in this folder because BFL is a wholesale-funded NBFC (deposits only 14% of borrowings) with a largely unsecured/semi-secured consumer and SME book and a history of RBI product-level action (eCOM/Insta EMI Card, Nov-2023 to May-2024). Bull 12.5%, bear 14.0%. No net-debt deduction: these are post-interest equity flows.
inputs.lease_treatment: Ind AS 116 lease depreciation and interest (lease liabilities Rs 1,163cr at FY26) are inside PBT; lease_cost_pct_path = 0, da_pct_path = 0 so nothing is added back. D&A (Rs 1,009cr) stays inside the margin because the retention line replaces capex for a lender.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows. The margin paths are PBT to owners / total income, i.e. the ~13% minority in Bajaj Housing Finance (Rs 315cr of FY26 PAT, ~1.6%) is removed in the margin, not in the bridge, so NCI is charged exactly once.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity for a deposit-taking NBFC, run through the Drivers engine the same way as HDB/IBN (dcf-methods SKILL.md routing row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker, thrift'; first valuation of this ticker, no prior model to match). An owner-FCF DCF is meaningless here: reported OCF is -Rs 658bn because loan originations sit in operating cash flow, and borrowings are the raw material. Engine mapping: revenue = consolidated total income; ebitda_margin_path = PBT to owners + SBC, as % of total income (pre-SBC so the engine's SBC deduction lands once); sbc_pct_path = SBC % of income; da = lease = 0; cash_tax_rate = 25.2% (FY26 effective 25.1%, H1 FY27 25.4%); capex_pct_path = equity retention kappa x g/(1+g); wc = 0; wacc = INR cost of equity; terminal growth 6.0% base (below India nominal GDP ~10%, above the 6.5% used for the large private banks' bull case). Terminal_cap_multiple 18x FCFE never binds (Gordon at 13%/6% = 15.1x). Growth is faded to within 50bp of terminal growth by year 10 so the year-10 retention is terminal-consistent. SBC-zero does not apply (ESOP ~0.5% of income), but house and street bases differ by only ~2%.

bear.capex_rationale: Equity retention = 150 x g/(1+g) percent of revenue (kappa 1.50: RBI scale-based rules or a credit event force leverage below 5x and a further dilutive raise).
bear.narrative: An Indian consumer-credit downturn in FY28-29 (unsecured, MFI and gold-loan stress) takes loan losses to ~2.3-2.5% of AUF (FY21-22 analogue) and growth to single digits for two years; banks, fintechs and captive financiers permanently compress spreads in durables and personal loans, so PBT margin recovers only to 31% (ROE ~14-15%). Regulatory risk (NBFC-UL rules, a repeat digital-lending ban) is charged in a 14% cost of equity and 5% perpetual growth.

base.growth_rationale: Total income, not AUM. FY27 +21% (H1 +21.3%; management raised FY27 AUM guidance to 26-27%, revenue lags by ~5 pts on repo-cut repricing and mortgage mix). AUM corridor 23-25% then fades as the franchise matures toward system credit growth (~12-13%); income growth fades to 6.5% by FY36, within 50bp of terminal growth. Implies FY36 total income ~Rs 2.73trn, AUM ~Rs 18-19 lakh crore.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC PBT to owners as % of total income. FY26 reported 31.5% (adjusted 33.7%), H1 FY27 35.0% before NCI (~34.4% after). Components held near today: interest expense ~35% of income (mortgage mix offsets rate cuts), opex ~21% (33% of NTI, guided -25-40bp/yr from FINAI), loan losses ~10% of income (loan loss/AUF ~1.7%, mid-cycle between FY23's 0.96% and FY26's 2.09%), NCI ~1.6% of PAT. ROE on average equity ~20% near term, ~18% terminal.
base.capex_rationale: Equity retention = 140 x g/(1+g) percent of revenue (kappa 1.40 = owners' equity / total income, FY26 actual 1.39, leverage corridor 5.0-5.5x). Terminal-consistent retention at 6% growth would be 7.9%; year-10 at 6.5% growth is 8.54%, slightly conservative.
base.narrative: Franchise compounds as guided: AUM 23-25% corridor for 3-4 years, ROA 4.3-4.7%, ROE 19-21%, GNPA <1.4%, opex leverage from FINAI, with growth fading toward system credit growth by the mid-2030s. The Oct-2026 raise funds the FY27-28 book; thereafter retention is funded from profit. Near-zero FCFE in FY27 is the price of 21% growth at a 5x leverage cap.

bull.capex_rationale: Equity retention = 135 x g/(1+g) percent of revenue (kappa 1.35: leverage run at the 5.5x top of the corridor).
bull.narrative: Income grows in line with the raised 26-27% AUM guidance less a smaller yield drag; credit costs settle at the 1.3-1.5% vintage trend management points to; FINAI delivers 100bp+ of opex/NTI leverage; ROA holds 4.7% and ROE 21%+. Cost of equity 12.5% (bank parity) as the deposit franchise and AAA ratings narrow the NBFC-vs-bank funding gap; 6.5% perpetual growth.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the house 15% to 25%: a largely unsecured/semi-secured book at the top of an Indian consumer-credit upcycle (Stage 2&3 ticked up to 2.02% in Q2 FY27), wholesale funding, a live regulatory record (Nov-2023 RBI product ban), promoter-board changes (Rajiv Bajaj exit Jul-2026) and the second dilutive raise in three years. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: the bull case requires growth, margin, credit cost and a lower cost of equity to all hold for a decade. Base 50%: a 19-year record of 33% income compounding, AAA ratings, GNPA 1.06% and management guidance that has been met or beaten make the framework the central case.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
